tickerNote: Wednesday 25 Nov closes. US markets are shut on Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early on Friday

lead.headline: Wall Street Claws Back From a 1,100-Point Dow Plunge as Hot Inflation Locks In a December Hike
lead.deck: The Nasdaq was down as much as 4.6% before a late rebound. Core PCE came in above forecasts, and Washington proposed new tariffs on 14 economies, India among them.
body: US stocks swung wildly on Wednesday before ending mixed. The Dow fell more than 1,100 points at its low, then closed up 164 points, or 0.33%, at 50,182.95. The S&P 500 had been down as much as 3.2% and finished 0.25% lower at 7,182.78, while the Nasdaq trimmed a 4.6% intraday slide to a 0.62% loss at 23,585.80.

The trigger was inflation. The PCE price index rose 3.8% in October from a year earlier, and the core measure rose 3.3%, a little above the 3.2% consensus. Core prices rose 0.3% for a third straight month. Markets priced the chance of a December Fed rate hike at roughly 93–98%. Treasury yields still eased, with the 10-year down about 6 basis points to 4.85%, and third-quarter GDP was revised up to 4.3% annualised.

The AI sell-off continued underneath. Nvidia fell 3.91% and is down 27% for November, after S&P Global put its AA credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade over governance concerns tied to Jensen Huang's brief ouster and return. Oracle lost 5.1%, Micron 4.5% and Sandisk 5.6%. Energy led the sectors as Brent jumped 3.5% to $94.61 after Houthi forces said they struck Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery.

Trade added to the uncertainty. The US Trade Representative proposed new Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies over what it calls structural excess capacity, with rates of up to 25% for India and up to 20% for China. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC the duties are likely months away and should not fully stack on existing ones. US markets are closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving.

top: The Dow erased a 1,100-point drop to close higher, but hot core PCE inflation cemented bets on a December Fed hike.
The US proposed new Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, with rates of up to 25% for India; comments are due 5 January.
S&P Global put Nvidia's AA credit rating on watch for a downgrade over board oversight and succession risk.
Sensex jumped 1,502 points and the Nifty 1.85% on foreign buying and FMCG strength, a day after Asia's AI rout.
Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness fund told investors it lost 65% in the third quarter, the WSJ reported.

items.fig: Core PCE +3.3% y/y · Headline +3.8% · Q3 GDP revised to 4.3%
items.headline: Inflation Runs Hot, Hike Bets Firm Up
items.body: October's PCE data came in slightly above expectations, leaving futures pricing a December rate hike as near-certain. Yields still fell, with the 2-year at 4.61% and the 10-year at 4.85%.

items.headline: Indian Stocks Roar Back After the Holiday
items.body: Private banks, financials and consumer staples led the rebound, helped by foreign buying and softer crude in Asian hours. Metals and media lagged, and the smallcap index slipped 0.44%.

items.headline: Europe Gives Up Early Gains
items.body: European shares opened higher on autos and consumer names but turned lower as the AI sell-off on Wall Street deepened and the US inflation print hardened rate-hike expectations.

items.headline: Asia's Chipmakers Tumble, Oil Jumps
items.body: Samsung fell 9.9%, SK Hynix 10.3% and SoftBank 14.8% as the AI rout hit Asia. Oil rallied after the reported attack on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery.

items.headline: S&P Puts Nvidia's Rating on Watch
items.body: The agency cited board independence and key-man risk after Huang's ouster and reinstatement, and cut its governance assessment to neutral. Moody's left its rating unchanged.

items.headline: HP Leads the Day's Gainers
items.body: HP beat fiscal fourth-quarter estimates, gave an upbeat outlook and raised its dividend. Deere rose despite an earnings miss and a soft 2027 forecast, lifting fellow farm-equipment maker CNH.

items.headline: Weak Guidance Sinks Ambarella and Nutanix
items.body: Ambarella's revenue guidance fell far short, which it tied to memory-chip shortages. Nutanix guided below forecasts and announced CEO Rajiv Ramaswami's planned exit, and Urban Outfitters missed on comparable sales.

items.fig: HUL, Tata Consumer, Nestle India among top Nifty gainers
items.headline: Staples Lead Mumbai, Steelmakers Lag
items.body: Hindustan Unilever, Tata Consumer and HDFC Life were among the Nifty's best performers. Tata Steel, Hindalco and JSW Steel were among the weakest as the metal index fell 2%.

items.headline: Eldridge-Led Group Agrees to Take Over Lukoil's Foreign Assets
items.body: A US-led consortium will swap restricted Russian shares for all of Lukoil International, which operates in 11 countries. The deal needs OFAC approval, and the proceeds will sit in a restricted account until sanctions lift or five years pass.

items.fig: 5 directors per side · Morgan Stanley, Goldman, Evercore advising
items.headline: Tesla and SpaceX Form Merger Committees
items.body: Both boards have set up special committees to negotiate a possible all-stock combination, Reuters reported, though no deal has been agreed. Defence contracts and Tesla's exposure to China could draw regulatory scrutiny.

items.headline: Vivakor to Buy Direct Midstream
items.body: The energy services company disclosed an agreement to acquire all of the membership interests in Direct Midstream.

items.fig: Q3 −65% after fees · +88.5% year to September
items.headline: Situational Awareness Reveals a Brutal Quarter
items.body: Leopold Aschenbrenner's AI-focused fund told investors it nearly collapsed in the summer on leveraged bets, according to the Wall Street Journal. It has reshaped its portfolio and is hiring a chief risk officer.

items.fig: SOFR call open interest +1.3 m contracts in November
items.headline: Funds Hedge Against a Fed Overshoot
items.body: Hedge funds are buying protection against the risk that rate hikes hurt growth and force the Fed back to easing, Hedgeweek reported, citing Bloomberg. Treasury options positioning has tilted toward calls.

items.fig: India up to 25% · 17% with a trade pact · China up to 20%
items.headline: US Proposes Overcapacity Tariffs on 14 Economies
items.body: The USTR's Section 301 plan covers China, the EU, Japan and India, with public comments due by 5 January 2027. Greer said the duties are largely already expected by trading partners and are unlikely to start for a couple of months.

items.fig: ~₹297 cr · Series A · led by A91 Partners
items.headline: AidenAI Raises About $32 Million
items.body: The enterprise AI startup closed one of the larger Indian rounds of the day. Separately, JioStar carried out a second round of layoffs, Inc42 reported.

items.headline: PayU India Turns Profitable on an Adjusted Basis
items.body: The payments firm reported positive adjusted EBITDA for the first half of the fiscal year. US firm VU Venture Partners also entered India, with seed and Series A cheques of $100,000 to $1 million.

items.headline: Silver Jewellery Brand Zavya Raises Funds
items.body: The Gurugram D2C brand's round was led by Daksham Growth Ventures. Skincare brand Numour is reportedly in talks to raise about $3.1 million led by Sharrp Ventures.
